summary:
AstroVital is a web-based astronaut health-monitoring system that turns continuous vital-sign data into a clear, explained status: NORMAL, WATCH or ATTENTION. It tracks respiratory rate, blood oxygen, blood pressure, heart rate, skin temperature and glucose.  It shows live charts and 7-day and 30-day trends, and gives the crew green, yellow or red guidance on what to do next.
It addresses the challenge by judging each reading in context instead of against one fixed limit. Every status combines safe ranges adjusted for microgravity, the astronaut’s current activity, how long a value has persisted, and the astronaut’s own baseline from a pre-flight calibration period and microgravity analogs. This cuts false alarms during exercise and catches changes that are normal for one person but not for another.
This matters because astronauts on long missions, far from immediate medical help, need fast, trustworthy, personalized health insight. AstroVital gives crew and flight surgeons actionable answers rather than raw numbers. It is a working prototype built on a secure, role-based platform and ready to connect to real sensors.
details:
ASTROVITAL

WHAT IT IS
AstroVital is a web-based astronaut health-monitoring and decision-support application. It organises and interprets physiological measurements associated with the Bio-Monitor wearable system, presents them on one dashboard, compares them with each astronaut’s own baseline, tracks changes over time and highlights readings that may need closer attention. The prototype uses synthetic data generated with Claude AI. It has not been connected to an operational ISS Bio-Monitor device.

HOW IT WORKS
Astronauts sign in with a crew ID and passcode or a passkey, and every page requires sign-in. Readings arrive every few seconds for six measurements: heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO2), skin temperature and physical activity. Each reading is assessed using safe ranges, the astronaut’s current activity, how long a deviation has lasted and the astronaut’s personal baseline. The dashboard shows a status of NORMAL (green), WATCH (yellow) or ATTENTION (red), with an explanation and advice on what to do. Daily averages show 7-day and 30-day trends. The prototype interface also carries blood glucose and scheduled ultrasound entries that sit outside the core six-measurement scope.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT
Crew and flight surgeons get a clear, explained status instead of raw numbers. Taking activity into account reduces false alarms, for example a high breathing rate during exercise. Baseline comparison highlights changes that are unusual for that astronaut, even when they fall inside a general range. The intended impact is to support faster, more personalised health decisions on long missions, where medical help is far away.

CREATIVITY
The project judges each astronaut against their own normal rather than a one-size-fits-all limit. It treats exercise as context and turns numbers into a colour-coded status with a reason and advice. The simulator varies readings realistically around each astronaut’s baseline, so the demo shows NORMAL, WATCH and ATTENTION changes.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY
Frontend: HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Interface design: Figma.

Development: Visual Studio Code.

Backend: Node.js, TypeScript and Express, with Prisma.

Database: PostgreSQL hosted on Neon.

Security: hashed passcodes, secure session cookies and WebAuthn passkeys. Testing: vitest.

Deployment: Vercel (also configured for Render with Docker).

Synthetic data: generated with Claude AI.

No physical hardware was used, and a built-in simulator stands in for the Bio-Monitor.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED
Differences between astronauts and between Earth and microgravity. Reducing false alarms while still catching real changes. The security and privacy of health data, with astronauts seeing only their own records. A clear display for crew under pressure. NASA Human Research Program material on 6-degree Head-Down Tilt Bed Rest informed our case to mimic space weather conditions to establish personalised baselines on earth. We use it as a design reference only and do not claim to run that protocol.

LIMITATIONS
Data is synthetic, and the system is not connected to a real Bio-Monitor. Statuses are software-generated decision-support indicators, not medical diagnoses. Thresholds and algorithms need expert validation before any operational or clinical use. Future work includes integrating with compatible wearable hardware and validating the logic with domain experts.

TEAM
